svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.9.10.1 Egress Windows or Doors for Bedrooms
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.10.1 Egress Windows or Doors for Bedrooms
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Egress Windows or Doors for Bedrooms

g.text: Bedroom window: openable from the inside
without keys, tools or special knowledge
SENTENCE (2) AND NOTE A-9.9.10.1.(2): WINDOW OPENING AREAS AND DIMENSIONS
Required: 0.35 m² (3.8 ft²) min., no dimension less than 380 mm (14 15/16″).

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Each bedroom or combination bedroom has at least one
outside window or exterior door openable from the inside
without keys, tools or special knowledge, and without
removing sashes or hardware
Except where the suite is sprinklered. See Article 9.5.1.2.
The window provides an unobstructed opening of not less
than 0.35 m² (3.8 ft²) with no dimension less than 380
mm (14 15/16″), and keeps that opening during an
emergency without additional support
Where the window opens into a window well, a clearance
of not less than 760 mm (29 15/16″) is provided in front
of it
Where the sash swings towards the window well, its
operation does not reduce the clearance in a way that
would restrict escape
A protective enclosure over the window well is openable
from the inside without keys, tools or special knowledge
of the opening mechanism
Notes
The opening must be achievable with the normal operating
procedure. Sills of escape windows are recommended to be not
higher than 1.5 m above the floor. For outward-opening
awnings, the 760 mm is needed beyond the outer edge of the
sash.
Drawn: a basement bedroom window opening into a window well. Soil and the front of the well are cut away.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.10.1. (page 9-55), with Notes A-9.9.10.1.(1) to (3).
